units.zh: 語曰：「世亂識忠臣。」
units.en: The proverb says: "In chaos, loyal ministers stand revealed."
units.literal: The saying goes: "In a chaotic age one knows loyal ministers."

units.zh: 誠哉！
units.en: How true that is!
units.literal: How true!

units.zh: 五代之際，不可以為無人，吾得全節之士三人焉，作《死節傳》。
units.en: The Five Dynasties were not without men of worth. I have found three who died with their integrity intact—and so I write this "Biography of Martyrs to Virtue."
units.literal: In the age of the Five Dynasties one cannot say there were no men of worth. I have found three who kept their integrity whole, and compose this "Biography of Martyrs to Virtue."

units.zh: 王彥章
units.en: Wang Yanzhang
units.literal: Wang Yanzhang

units.zh: 〈（裴約 劉仁贍附）〉
units.en: (Pei Yue and Liu Renzhan appended)
units.literal: (Pei Yue and Liu Renzhan appended)

units.zh: 王彥章，字子明，鄆州壽張人也。
units.en: Wang Yanzhang, styled Ziming, came from Shouzhang in Yun Prefecture.
units.literal: Wang Yanzhang, styled Ziming, was a native of Shouzhang in Yun Prefecture.

units.zh: 少為軍卒，事梁太祖，為開封府押衙、左親從指揮使、行營先鋒馬軍使。
units.en: He began as a common soldier under Liang Taizu, rising to Kaifeng escort officer, commander of the Left Personal Followers, and vanguard cavalry commander on campaign.
units.literal: In youth he was a common soldier. He served Liang Taizu as Kaifeng Intendant escort officer, Left Personal Followers commander, and vanguard cavalry commander on campaign.

units.zh: 末帝即位，遷濮州刺史，又徙澶州刺史。
units.en: When the Last Emperor took the throne, he became prefect of Pu, then of Chan.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor acceded, he was moved to prefect of Pu, then transferred to prefect of Chan.

units.zh: 彥章為人驍勇有力，能跣足履棘行百步。
units.en: Yanzhang was fierce and strong enough to walk a hundred paces barefoot over thorns.
units.literal: Yanzhang was fierce, brave, and strong; he could walk a hundred paces barefoot over thorns.

units.zh: 持一鐵槍，騎而馳突，奮疾如飛，而佗人莫能舉也，軍中號王鐵槍。
units.en: He wielded an iron spear no other man could lift. Mounted, he charged like a gale. The army called him Wang Iron Spear.
units.literal: He carried an iron spear; mounted, he charged and broke through like a gale—yet no other man could lift it. The army called him Wang Iron Spear.

units.zh: 梁、晉爭天下為勁敵，獨彥章心常輕晉王，謂人曰：「亞次鬥雞小兒耳，何足懼哉！」
units.en: Liang and Jin were mortal rivals, yet Yanzhang alone always scorned the Prince of Jin. "That second-rate cockfighting brat," he said—"what is there to fear?"
units.literal: Liang and Jin were bitter rivals for the realm, yet Yanzhang alone always looked down on the Prince of Jin, telling others: "That second-rank cockfighting boy—what is there to fear!"

units.zh: 梁分魏、相六州為兩鎮，懼魏軍不從，遣彥章將五百騎入魏，屯金波亭以虞變。
units.en: Liang split Wei and Xiang into two commands. Fearing mutiny among the Wei troops, they sent Yanzhang with five hundred cavalry into Wei and camped at Jinbo Pavilion to watch for trouble.
units.literal: Liang split the six prefectures of Wei and Xiang into two commands. Fearing the Wei troops would not obey, they sent Yanzhang with five hundred horsemen into Wei, encamped at Jinbo Pavilion to guard against trouble.

units.zh: 魏軍果亂，夜攻彥章。
units.en: The Wei army did rebel and attacked Yanzhang by night.
units.literal: The Wei army did rebel and attacked Yanzhang by night.

units.zh: 彥章南走，魏人降晉。
units.en: Yanzhang fled south; the Wei men went over to Jin.
units.literal: Yanzhang fled south; the Wei men surrendered to Jin.

units.zh: 晉軍攻破澶州，虜彥章妻子歸之太原，賜以第宅，供給甚備，間遣使者招彥章，彥章斬其使者以自絕。
units.en: Jin took Chan Prefecture, carried Yanzhang’s family to Taiyuan, gave them a mansion and rich provision, and sent envoys now and then to win him over. Yanzhang killed every envoy and broke for good.
units.literal: The Jin army took Chan Prefecture, carried off Yanzhang’s wife and children to Taiyuan, granted them a mansion, and supplied them generously. From time to time they sent envoys to win Yanzhang over; Yanzhang executed the envoys to cut himself off.

units.zh: 然晉人畏彥章之在梁也，必欲招致之，待其妻子愈厚。
units.en: Jin feared Yanzhang as long as he served Liang and was bent on winning him—they treated his family even more generously.
units.literal: Yet the Jin feared Yanzhang while he remained with Liang and were determined to win him; they treated his wife and children all the more generously.

units.zh: 自梁失魏、博，與晉夾河而軍，彥章常為先鋒。
units.en: Once Liang lost Wei and Bo, the two powers faced each other across the Yellow River—and Yanzhang was always in the vanguard.
units.literal: After Liang lost Wei and Bo, its armies faced Jin across the river; Yanzhang was always in the vanguard.

units.zh: 遷汝鄭二州防禦使、匡國軍節度使、北面行營副招討使，又徙宣義軍節度使。
units.en: He rose to defender of Ru and Zheng, governor of Kuangguo, deputy northern campaign commissioner, then governor of Xuanyi.
units.literal: He was promoted to defender of Ru and Zheng, military governor of the Kuangguo Army, deputy northern campaign commissioner, then transferred to military governor of the Xuanyi Army.

units.zh: 是時，晉已盡有河北，以鐵鎖斷德勝口，築河南、北為兩城，號「夾寨」。
units.en: By then Jin held all Hebei. They chained off Desheng Crossing and built twin cities north and south of the river—the "Pincer Forts."
units.literal: By then Jin held all of Hebei. They blocked Desheng Crossing with iron chains and built north and south cities on the river—called the "Twin Forts."

units.zh: 而梁末帝昏亂，小人趙巖、張漢傑等用事，大臣宿將多被讒間，彥章雖為招討副使，而謀不見用。
units.en: The Last Emperor was lost; Zhao Yan and Zhang Hanjie ran the court, and veteran ministers and generals were slandered aside. Yanzhang was deputy campaign commander, but no one listened.
units.literal: The Last Emperor was muddled; petty men Zhao Yan and Zhang Hanjie held power, and veteran ministers and generals were slandered out of favor. Though Yanzhang was deputy campaign commissioner, his counsel went unused.

units.zh: 龍德三年夏，晉取鄆州，梁人大恐，宰相敬翔顧事急，以繩內靴中，入見末帝，泣曰：「先帝取天下，不以臣為不肖，所謀無不用。
units.en: Summer, Longde year three: Jin took Yun Prefecture and Liang panicked. Chancellor Jing Xiang, seeing ruin close, hid a rope in his boot, went before the Last Emperor, and wept: "The Founder took the realm and never thought me unworthy—every plan of mine was used.
units.literal: In summer of Longde year three Jin took Yun Prefecture. Liang was terrified. Chancellor Jing Xiang, seeing affairs desperate, hid a rope in his boot, entered to see the Last Emperor, and wept: "The Founding Emperor took the realm and did not think me unworthy—none of my counsel went unused.

units.zh: 今強敵未滅，陛下棄忽臣言，臣身不用，不如死！」
units.en: The great enemy still stands, yet Your Majesty ignores me. If I am useless, I would rather die!"
units.literal: Now the great foe is not destroyed, yet Your Majesty casts aside my words and will not employ me—I would rather die!"

units.zh: 乃引繩將自經。
units.en: He drew the rope to hang himself.
units.literal: He then drew the rope to hang himself.

units.zh: 末帝使人止之，問所欲言。
units.en: The Last Emperor stopped him and asked what he had to say.
units.literal: The Last Emperor sent men to stop him and asked what he wished to say.

units.zh: 翔曰：「事急矣，非彥章不可！」
units.en: Xiang said: "It is desperate—only Yanzhang can save us!"
units.literal: Xiang said: "Affairs are desperate—only Yanzhang will do!"

units.zh: 末帝乃召彥章為招討使，以段凝為副。
units.en: The Last Emperor summoned Yanzhang as campaign commander and made Duan Ning his deputy.
units.literal: The Last Emperor then summoned Yanzhang as campaign commissioner and made Duan Ning his deputy.

units.zh: 末帝問破敵之期，彥章對曰：「三日。」
units.en: The Last Emperor asked when he could break the enemy. Yanzhang said: "Three days."
units.literal: The Last Emperor asked when the enemy could be broken; Yanzhang answered: "Three days."

units.zh: 左右皆失笑。
units.en: Everyone around him laughed out loud.
units.literal: Those around all burst out laughing.

units.zh: 彥章受命而出，馳兩日至滑州，置酒大會，陰遣人具舟於楊村，命甲士六百人皆持巨斧，載冶者，具韝炭，乘流而下。
units.en: Yanzhang took command and rode. Two days later he was at Hua Prefecture, feasting while secretly preparing boats at Yang Village—six hundred armored men with great axes, smiths with bellows and charcoal, all drifting downstream.
units.literal: Yanzhang took the commission and rode out. In two days he reached Hua Prefecture, held a great feast, and secretly had boats prepared at Yang Village. Six hundred armored men each carried great axes; smiths came with bellows and charcoal, and all floated downstream.

units.zh: 彥章會飲，酒半，佯起更衣，引精兵數千，沿河以趨德勝。
units.en: Mid-feast he pretended to leave and change clothes, then led several thousand picked troops along the river toward Desheng.
units.literal: At the feast, halfway through the wine, he pretended to rise and change clothes, then led several thousand picked troops along the river toward Desheng.

units.zh: 舟兵舉鎖燒斷之，因以巨斧斬浮橋，而彥章引兵急擊南城。
units.en: The boatmen burned through the chains, smashed the floating bridge with great axes, and Yanzhang stormed the south city.
units.literal: The boatmen raised the chains, burned through them, then hewed the floating bridge with great axes; Yanzhang led his troops in a furious assault on the south city.

units.zh: 浮橋斷，南城遂破，蓋三日矣。
units.en: The bridge broke, the south city fell—and it had been three days.
units.literal: The bridge was severed and the south city fell—it had been three days.

units.zh: 是時莊宗在魏，以朱守殷守夾寨，聞彥章為招討使，驚曰：「彥章驍勇，吾嘗避其鋒，非守殷敵也。
units.en: Zhuangzong was at Wei; Zhu Shouyin held the Twin Forts. Hearing Yanzhang had command, he said in alarm: "Yanzhang is fierce—I have always dodged his spear. Shouyin cannot stand against him.
units.literal: Zhuangzong was then at Wei; Zhu Shouyin held the Twin Forts. Hearing Yanzhang was campaign commander, he said in alarm: "Yanzhang is fierce—I have always avoided his edge. Shouyin is no match.

units.zh: 然彥章兵少，利於速戰，必急攻我南城。」
units.en: But his force is small. He lives by speed—and he will hit our south city at once."
units.literal: Yet Yanzhang’s troops are few; he thrives on speed and will surely strike our south city at once."

units.zh: 即馳騎救之，行二十里，而得夾寨報者曰：「彥章兵已至。」
units.en: He galloped to the rescue. Twenty li out a messenger from the Twin Forts cried: "Yanzhang is here!"
units.literal: He immediately galloped to the rescue. Twenty li out a messenger from the Twin Forts reported: "Yanzhang’s army has arrived."

units.zh: 比至，而南城破矣。
units.en: By the time he arrived, the south city was already lost.
units.literal: By the time he arrived, the south city had already fallen.

units.zh: 莊宗徹北城為筏，下楊劉，與彥章俱浮於河，各行一岸，每舟抃相及輒戰，一日數十接。
units.en: Zhuangzong broke up the north city into rafts and floated down to Yang Liu. He and Yanzhang raced along opposite banks; whenever a boat came within reach they fought—dozens of clashes in a single day.
units.literal: Zhuangzong dismantled the north city into rafts and floated down to Yang Liu. He and Yanzhang drifted on the river, each on one bank; whenever boats drew near they fought—dozens of clashes in a day.

units.zh: 彥章至楊劉，攻之幾下。
units.en: At Yang Liu Yanzhang nearly broke through.
units.literal: Yanzhang reached Yang Liu and nearly took it.

units.zh: 晉人築壘博州東岸，彥章引兵攻之，不克，還擊楊劉，戰敗。
units.en: Jin raised fortifications east of Bo Prefecture. Yanzhang attacked and failed, turned on Yang Liu, and was beaten.
units.literal: The Jin built fortifications on the east bank of Bo Prefecture. Yanzhang led troops against them but could not take them; he turned back to strike Yang Liu and was defeated.

units.zh: 是時，段凝已有異志，與趙巖、張漢傑交通，彥章素剛，憤梁日削，而嫉巖等所為，嘗謂人曰：「俟吾破賊還，誅奸臣以謝天下。」
units.en: By then Duan Ning was already playing a double game, dealing with Zhao Yan and Zhang Hanjie. Yanzhang was blunt; he watched Liang shrink day by day and hated the court’s petty men. He often said: "When I break the enemy and march home, I will kill the traitors and answer the realm."
units.literal: By then Duan Ning already harbored other designs. He trafficked with Zhao Yan and Zhang Hanjie. Yanzhang was blunt by nature; he raged as Liang shrank daily and hated what Zhao Yan and the rest were doing. He often told others: "Wait until I break the enemy and return—then I will execute the traitors to answer the realm."

units.zh: 巖等聞之懼，與凝葉力傾之。
units.en: Zhao Yan and the rest heard and were terrified; they and Ning united to destroy him.
units.literal: Zhao Yan and the rest heard and were afraid; with Ning they joined forces to bring him down.

units.zh: 其破南城也，彥章與凝各為捷書以聞，凝遣人告巖等匿彥章書而上己書，末帝初疑其事，已而使者至軍，獨賜勞凝而不及彥章，軍士皆失色。
units.en: When the south city fell, Yanzhang and Ning each sent victory dispatches. Ning’s men told Zhao Yan to bury Yanzhang’s report and push Ning’s instead. The Last Emperor doubted at first—then the envoy reached camp and rewards went to Ning alone. The soldiers went white.
units.literal: When the south city fell, Yanzhang and Ning each sent victory reports. Ning had men tell Zhao Yan and the rest to hide Yanzhang’s report and submit his own. At first the Last Emperor doubted; then when the envoy reached the army, rewards went to Ning alone and not to Yanzhang—the soldiers all turned pale.

units.zh: 及楊劉之敗也，凝乃上書言：「彥章使酒輕敵而至於敗。」
units.en: After Yang Liu, Ning wrote: "Yanzhang drank, scorned the enemy, and lost."
units.literal: After the defeat at Yang Liu, Ning memorialized: "Yanzhang drank and despised the enemy, and so was defeated."

units.zh: 趙巖等從中日夜毀之，乃罷彥章，以凝為招討使。
units.en: Zhao Yan and the rest tore at him day and night. Yanzhang was stripped of command; Ning took his place.
units.literal: Zhao Yan and the rest slandered him day and night; Yanzhang was removed and Ning made campaign commissioner.

units.zh: 彥章馳至京師入見，以笏畫地，自陳勝敗之跡，巖等諷有司劾彥章不恭，勒還第。
units.en: Yanzhang raced to the capital and laid the battle out on the floor with his tablet. Zhao Yan and the rest had the authorities charge him with disrespect and send him home.
units.literal: Yanzhang galloped to the capital and entered audience. With his tablet he traced the ground, recounting the course of victory and defeat. Zhao Yan and the rest hinted that the authorities should impeach Yanzhang for disrespect and order him back to his mansion.

units.zh: 唐兵攻兗州，末帝召彥章使守捉東路。
units.en: Tang attacked Yan Prefecture; the Last Emperor called Yanzhang to hold the eastern road.
units.literal: Tang troops attacked Yan Prefecture; the Last Emperor summoned Yanzhang to guard the eastern route.

units.zh: 是時，梁之勝兵皆屬段凝，京師只有保鑾五百騎，皆新捉募之兵，不可用，乃以屬彥章，而以張漢傑監之。
units.en: Liang’s best troops were all with Duan Ning. The capital had only five hundred Palace Guard cavalry—raw recruits, good for nothing. These were handed to Yanzhang, with Zhang Hanjie watching over him.
units.literal: By then Liang’s best troops all belonged to Duan Ning; the capital had only five hundred Palace Guard cavalry—all newly drafted and useless. These were given to Yanzhang, with Zhang Hanjie to oversee him.

units.zh: 彥章至遞坊，以兵少戰敗，退保中都；
units.en: At Difang Yanzhang was too weak to win; he fell back on Zhongdu;
units.literal: Yanzhang reached Difang. Too few to fight, he was beaten and fell back on Zhongdu;

units.zh: 又敗，與其牙兵百餘騎死戰。
units.en: beaten again, he and a little over a hundred of his personal troops fought to the death.
units.literal: beaten again, he and a little over a hundred of his personal troops fought to the death.

units.zh: 唐將夏魯奇素與彥章善，識其語音，曰：「王鐵槍也！」
units.en: The Tang general Xia Luqi had served with Yanzhang and knew his voice. He shouted: "Wang Iron Spear!"
units.literal: The Tang general Xia Luqi had long been on good terms with Yanzhang and knew his voice. He cried: "Wang Iron Spear!"

units.zh: 舉槊刺之，彥章傷重，馬踣，被擒。
units.en: He drove his spear into him. Yanzhang was gravely wounded, his horse went down, and he was taken.
units.literal: He thrust with his spear; Yanzhang was gravely wounded, his horse collapsed, and he was captured.

units.zh: 莊宗見之，曰：「爾常以孺子待我，今日服乎？」
units.en: Zhuangzong looked at him and said: "You always called me a stripling—are you satisfied now?"
units.literal: Zhuangzong saw him and said: "You always treated me as a stripling—are you satisfied today?"

units.zh: 又曰：「爾善戰者，何不守兗州而守中都？
units.en: He asked again: "They say you are a master of war—why hold Zhongdu instead of Yan Prefecture?
units.literal: He said again: "They say you are skilled in war—why hold Zhongdu and not Yan Prefecture?

units.zh: 中都無壁壘，何以自固？」
units.en: Zhongdu has no walls. How could you hold it?"
units.literal: Zhongdu has no walls—how could you make yourself secure?"

units.zh: 彥章對曰：「大事已去，非人力可為！」
units.en: Yanzhang said: "The cause is lost. No human strength can mend it!"
units.literal: Yanzhang answered: "The great affair is already lost; it is not within human power to mend!"

units.zh: 莊宗惻然，賜藥以封其創。
units.en: Zhuangzong was moved and sent medicine to bind his wounds.
units.literal: Zhuangzong was moved and sent medicine to dress his wound.

units.zh: 彥章武人不知書，常為俚語謂人曰：「豹死留皮，人死留名。」
units.en: Yanzhang could not read, but he had a saying: "The leopard dies and leaves its hide; the man dies and leaves his name."
units.literal: Yanzhang was a soldier who did not know books; he often used a common saying: "When the leopard dies it leaves its pelt; when a man dies he leaves his name."

units.zh: 其於忠義，蓋天性也。
units.en: Loyalty and righteousness were in his bones.
units.literal: In loyalty and righteousness, it was his nature.

units.zh: 莊宗愛其驍勇，欲全活之，使人慰諭彥章，彥章謝曰：「臣與陛下血戰十餘年，今兵敗力窮，不死何待？
units.en: Zhuangzong admired his valor and wanted to save him. He sent men to win him over. Yanzhang refused: "I fought you in blood for more than ten years. Now my army is broken and my strength spent—if I do not die, what am I waiting for?
units.literal: Zhuangzong admired his fierceness and wished to spare him. He sent men to comfort and persuade Yanzhang. Yanzhang declined: "Your servant fought Your Majesty in blood for more than ten years. Now the army is broken and strength spent—if I do not die, what am I waiting for?

units.zh: 且臣受梁恩，非死不能報，豈有朝事梁而暮事晉，生何面目見天下之人乎！」
units.en: I owe Liang a debt only death can pay. Serve Liang at dawn and Jin at dusk? What face would I show the world!"
units.literal: Moreover I received Liang’s grace; only death can repay it. How could I serve Liang at dawn and Jin at dusk—what face would I have before the men of the realm!"

units.zh: 莊宗又遣明宗往諭之，彥章病創，臥不能起，仰顧明宗，呼其小字曰：「汝非邈佶烈乎？
units.en: Zhuangzong sent Mingzong to persuade him. Yanzhang’s wounds were too grave to rise. He looked up at Mingzong and called his childhood name: "Are you not Miaojilie?
units.literal: Zhuangzong again sent Mingzong to persuade him. Yanzhang’s wounds were grave; he could not rise. He looked up at Mingzong and called him by his childhood name: "Are you not Miaojilie?

units.zh: 我豈茍活者？」
units.en: Do you take me for a man who clings to life?"
units.literal: Do you think I am a man who clings to life?"

units.zh: 遂見殺，年六十一。
units.en: He was then killed—sixty-one years old.
units.literal: He was then executed—aged sixty-one.

units.zh: 晉高祖時，追贈彥章太師。
units.en: Under Jin Gaozu he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: Under Jin Gaozu he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 與彥章同時有裴約者，潞州之牙將也。
units.en: In Yanzhang’s day there was also Pei Yue, a staff officer of Luzhou.
units.literal: At the same time as Yanzhang there was Pei Yue, a staff officer of Luzhou.

units.zh: 莊宗以李嗣昭為昭義軍節度使，約以裨將守澤州。
units.en: Zhuangzong made Li Sizhao governor of Zhaoyi; Yue, a subordinate commander, held Ze Prefecture.
units.literal: Zhuangzong made Li Sizhao military governor of the Zhaoyi Army; Yue, as a subordinate general, held Ze Prefecture.

units.zh: 嗣昭卒，其子繼韜以澤、潞叛降於梁，約召其州人泣而諭曰：「吾事故使二十餘年，見其分財饗士，欲報梁仇，不幸早世。
units.en: When Sizhao died, his son Jitao rebelled with Ze and Lu and went over to Liang. Yue gathered the people, wept, and said: "I served our old commissioner more than twenty years. I watched him share spoils and feast his men, burning to avenge Liang—then he died too soon.
units.literal: When Sizhao died, his son Jitao rebelled with Ze and Lu and surrendered to Liang. Yue gathered the people of the prefecture, wept, and addressed them: "I served the former commissioner more than twenty years. I saw him divide spoils and feast his men, wishing to avenge Liang—then he died untimely.

units.zh: 今郎君父喪未葬，違背君親，吾能死於此，不能從以歸梁也！」
units.en: Now his father is not yet buried, and he turns against lord and kin. I can die here. I will not follow him to Liang!"
units.literal: Now the young master’s father lies unburied, yet he turns against lord and kin. I can die here—I cannot follow him back to Liang!"

units.zh: 眾皆感泣。
units.en: All wept.
units.literal: All were moved to tears.

units.zh: 梁遣董璋率兵圍之，約與州人拒守，求救於莊宗。
units.en: Liang sent Dong Zhang to besiege the city. Yue and the people held out and begged Zhuangzong for help.
units.literal: Liang sent Dong Zhang with troops to besiege the city. Yue and the people of the prefecture held out and sent to Zhuangzong for rescue.

units.zh: 是時，莊宗方與梁人戰河上，而已建大號，聞繼韜叛降梁，頗有憂色，及聞約獨不叛，喜曰：「吾於繼韜何薄？
units.en: Zhuangzong was fighting Liang on the river and had already taken imperial title. Jitao’s defection darkened his face—but hearing Yue alone had held firm, he said with joy: "What did I ever owe Jitao?
units.literal: At that time Zhuangzong was fighting Liang on the river and had already proclaimed his great title. Hearing Jitao had rebelled and surrendered to Liang, his face clouded; hearing Yue alone had not rebelled, he said with joy: "What did I owe Jitao?

units.zh: 於約何厚？
units.en: What did I owe Yue?
units.literal: What did I owe Yue?

units.zh: 而約能分逆順邪！」
units.en: Yet Yue knows loyalty from treason!"
units.literal: Yet Yue can tell loyalty from treason!"

units.zh: 顧符存審曰：「吾不惜澤州與梁，一州易得，約難得也。
units.en: He turned to Fu Cunjian and said: "I would give Liang Ze Prefecture without regret—one prefecture is cheap; Yue is not.
units.literal: He turned to Fu Cunjian and said: "I would not begrudge Ze Prefecture to Liang—a single prefecture is easy to come by; Yue is hard to find.

units.zh: 爾識機便，為我取約來。」
units.en: You know how to read the moment. Bring Yue to me."
units.literal: You know how to seize the moment—bring Yue to me."

units.zh: 存審以五千騎馳至遼州，而梁兵已破澤州，約見殺。
units.en: Cunjian raced with five thousand cavalry to Lia Prefecture—but Liang had already taken Ze and Yue was dead.
units.literal: Cunjian galloped with five thousand cavalry to Lia Prefecture, but Liang troops had already broken Ze Prefecture and Yue had been killed.

units.zh: 劉仁贍
units.en: Liu Renzhan
units.literal: Liu Renzhan

units.zh: 至周世宗時，又有劉仁贍者焉。
units.en: By Shizong’s day there was Liu Renzhan.
units.literal: By the time of Later Zhou Shizong there was also Liu Renzhan.

units.zh: 仁贍字守惠，彭城人也。
units.en: Renzhan, styled Shouhui, came from Pengcheng.
units.literal: Renzhan, styled Shouhui, was a native of Pengcheng.

units.zh: 父金，事楊行密，為濠、滁二州刺史，以驍勇知名。
units.en: His father Jin served Yang Xingmi as prefect of Hao and Chu and was famed for courage.
units.literal: His father Jin served Yang Xingmi as prefect of Hao and Chu and was known for fierceness and bravery.

units.zh: 仁贍為將，輕財重士，法令嚴肅，少略通兵書。
units.en: As a commander Renzhan was generous with his purse and loyal to his men, stern in discipline, and had read some military texts.
units.literal: As a commander Renzhan was light with wealth and heavy toward his men, strict in law, and had some grasp of military books.

units.zh: 事南唐，為左監門衛將軍、黃袁二州刺史，所至稱治。
units.en: He served Southern Tang as Left Gate Guard general and prefect of Huang and Yuan; everywhere he went men praised his rule.
units.literal: He served Southern Tang as Left Gate Guard general and prefect of Huang and Yuan; wherever he went he was praised for good governance.

units.zh: 李景使掌親軍，以為武昌軍節度使。
units.en: Li Jing put him in charge of the imperial guard and made him governor of Wuchang.
units.literal: Li Jing put him in charge of the personal guard and made him military governor of the Wuchang Army.

units.zh: 周師征淮，先遣李穀攻自壽春，景遣將劉彥貞拒周兵，以仁贍為清淮軍節度使，鎮壽州。
units.en: When Zhou marched on the Huai, Li Gu struck first from Shouchun. Jing sent Liu Yanzhen to meet the Zhou army and made Renzhan governor of Qinghuai, stationed at Shou.
units.literal: When Zhou troops marched on the Huai, they first sent Li Gu to attack from Shouchun. Jing dispatched General Liu Yanzhen to meet the Zhou army and made Renzhan military governor of the Qinghuai Army, stationed at Shou Prefecture.

units.zh: 李穀退守正陽浮橋，彥貞見周兵之卻，意其怯，急追之。
units.en: Li Gu fell back on the Zhengyang floating bridge. Yanzhen saw the Zhou retreat and took them for cowards; he chased hard.
units.literal: Li Gu fell back to hold the Zhengyang floating bridge. Yanzhen saw the Zhou army retreat and thought them cowards; he pressed the pursuit hotly.

units.zh: 仁贍以為不可，彥貞不聽，仁贍獨按兵城守。
units.en: Renzhan said it was folly; Yanzhen would not hear him. Renzhan alone kept his troops in the city.
units.literal: Renzhan thought it unwise; Yanzhen would not listen. Renzhan alone held his troops and guarded the city.

units.zh: 彥貞果敗於正陽。
units.en: Yanzhen was routed at Zhengyang.
units.literal: Yanzhen was indeed defeated at Zhengyang.

units.zh: 世宗攻壽州，圍之數重，以方舟載炮，自淝河中流擊其城；
units.en: Shizong besieged Shou, ring upon ring. He mounted catapults on barges and hammered the walls from midstream on the Fei;
units.literal: Shizong besieged Shou Prefecture, ring upon ring. He loaded catapults on barges and struck the city from midstream on the Fei River;

units.zh: 又束巨竹數十萬竿，上施版屋，號為「竹龍」，載甲士以攻之，又決其水砦入於淝河。
units.en: he bound hundreds of thousands of bamboo poles, roofed them with boards into "Bamboo Dragons," loaded armored men to assault the walls, and broke the water fortifications to flood the Fei.
units.literal: he also bound hundreds of thousands of great bamboo poles, roofed them with planking, called them "Bamboo Dragons," loaded armored men aboard to attack, and broke the water fortifications to pour into the Fei.

units.zh: 攻之百端，自正月至於四月不能下，而歲大暑，霖雨彌旬，周兵營寨水深數尺，淮、淝暴漲，炮舟竹龍皆飄南岸，為景兵所焚，周兵多死。
units.en: Every assault failed from the first month to the fourth. Heat hammered the land; rain fell ten days straight. Zhou camps stood knee-deep in water; the Huai and Fei rose in flood. Catapult barges and Bamboo Dragons drifted south and Jing’s men burned them; Zhou dead piled up.
units.literal: He tried every method of assault from the first month to the fourth and could not take the city. That year the heat was fierce; rain fell for ten days. Zhou camps stood in water several feet deep; the Huai and Fei surged. The catapult barges and Bamboo Dragons drifted to the south bank and were burned by Jing’s troops; many Zhou soldiers died.

units.zh: 世宗東趨濠梁，以李重進為廬、壽都招討使。
units.en: Shizong marched east to Hao Bridge and made Li Chongjin overall commander of Lu and Shou.
units.literal: Shizong marched east to Hao Bridge and made Li Chongjin overall commander of Lu and Shou.

units.zh: 景亦遣其元帥齊王景達等列砦紫金山下，為夾道以屬城中。
units.en: Jing sent his commander-in-chief Prince Qi Jingda to camp below Purple Gold Mountain and build a covered road into the city.
units.literal: Jing also sent his commander-in-chief, Prince Qi Jingda, and others to camp below Purple Gold Mountain and build a covered road linking the city.

units.zh: 而重進與張永德兩軍相疑不協，仁贍屢請出戰，景達不許，由是憤惋成疾。
units.en: Chongjin and Zhang Yongde distrusted each other and would not cooperate. Renzhan begged again and again to sally; Jingda refused—and resentment curdled into sickness.
units.literal: Chongjin and Zhang Yongde’s two armies distrusted each other and would not cooperate. Renzhan repeatedly asked to sally forth; Jingda refused—so resentment and grief turned to illness.

units.zh: 明年正月，世宗復至淮上，盡破紫金山砦，壞其夾道，景兵大敗，諸將往往見擒，而景之守將廣陵馮延魯、光州張紹、舒州周祚、泰州方訥、泗州範再遇等，或走或降，皆不能守，雖景君臣亦皆震懾，奉表稱臣，願割土地、輸貢賦，以效誠款，而仁贍獨堅守，不可下。
units.en: First month of the next year Shizong returned to the Huai, smashed the Purple Gold Mountain camps, broke the covered road, and routed Jing’s army. Generals fell one after another; Feng Yanlu of Guangling, Zhang Shao of Guang, Zhou Zuo of Shu, Fang Ne of Tai, Fan Zaiyu of Si—commanders fled or surrendered and could not hold. Jing king and court shook, sent tribute, ceded land, bowed as subjects—Renzhan alone held and would not yield.
units.literal: In the first month of the next year Shizong returned to the Huai, broke all the Purple Gold Mountain camps, destroyed the covered road, and routed Jing’s army badly. Generals were taken one after another; Jing’s defending commanders—Guangling’s Feng Yanlu, Guang Prefecture’s Zhang Shao, Shu Prefecture’s Zhou Zuo, Tai Prefecture’s Fang Ne, Si Prefecture’s Fan Zaiyu, and others—fled or surrendered and could not hold their posts. Though Jing, king and ministers alike, were shaken and submitted memorials calling themselves subjects, offering to cede land and pay tribute in proof of loyalty, Renzhan alone held firm and could not be taken.

units.zh: 世宗使景所遣使者孫晟等至城下示之，仁贍子崇諫幸其父病，謀與諸將出降，仁贍立命斬之，監軍使周廷構哭於中門救之，不得，於是士卒皆感泣，願以死守。
units.en: Shizong paraded Jing’s envoy Sun Sheng below the walls. Renzhan’s son Chongjian, seeing his father ill, plotted surrender with the generals. Renzhan ordered him killed on the spot. Supervisor Zhou Tinggou wept at the middle gate in vain; the soldiers wept and swore to die with the city.
units.literal: Shizong had Jing’s envoy Sun Sheng and others come below the walls to show them. Renzhan’s son Chongjian, taking advantage of his father’s illness, plotted with the generals to surrender. Renzhan immediately ordered him executed. Supervisor Zhou Tinggou wept at the middle gate to save him but could not; the soldiers all wept and vowed to die defending the city.

units.zh: 三月，仁贍病甚，已不知人，其副使孫羽詐為仁贍書，以城降。
units.en: Third month: Renzhan was dying and no longer knew anyone. His deputy Sun Yu forged a letter in his name and surrendered the city.
units.literal: In the third month Renzhan’s illness was grave; he no longer knew men. His deputy Sun Yu forged a letter in Renzhan’s name and surrendered the city.

units.zh: 世宗命舁仁贍至帳前，嘆嗟久之，賜以玉帶、御馬，復使入城養疾，是日卒。
units.en: Shizong had Renzhan carried to his tent, sighed a long while, gave him a jade belt and an imperial horse, and sent him back into the city to recover. He died that day.
units.literal: Shizong had Renzhan carried before his tent, sighed long, granted him a jade belt and an imperial horse, and sent him back into the city to recover from illness. That day he died.

units.zh: 制曰：「劉仁贍盡忠所事，抗節無虧，前代名臣，幾人可比！
units.en: An edict ran: "Liu Renzhan gave his lord full loyalty and held his integrity without stain. Of the famed ministers of old, how many can match him!
units.literal: An edict said: "Liu Renzhan gave full loyalty to his lord and held his integrity without stain. Of famous ministers in former ages, how many can compare!

units.zh: 予之南伐，得爾為多。」
units.en: In my southern campaign, winning you meant more than winning cities.”
units.literal: In my southern campaign, gaining you counted for much.”

units.zh: 乃拜仁贍檢校太尉兼中書令、天平軍節度使。
units.en: He then made Renzhan Acting Grand Commandant and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and Military Governor of the Tianping Army.
units.literal: He then appointed Renzhan Acting Grand Commandant and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat and Military Governor of the Tianping Army.

units.zh: 仁贍不能受命而卒，年五十八。
units.en: Renzhan died before he could take up the post. He was fifty-eight.
units.literal: Renzhan could not accept the appointment before he died, at the age of fifty-eight.

units.zh: 世宗遣使吊祭，喪事官給，追封彭城郡王，以其子崇贊為懷州刺史，賜莊宅各一區。
units.en: Shizong sent envoys to mourn him and pay for the funeral from the treasury. He was posthumously made Prince of Pengcheng; his son Chongzan was named prefect of Huaizhou, and father and son each received an estate.
units.literal: Shizong sent envoys to offer condolences and sacrifices; funeral expenses were supplied by the state. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Pengcheng. His son Chongzan was made prefect of Huaizhou, and each was granted an estate.

units.zh: 李景聞仁贍卒，亦贈太師。
units.en: When Li Jing heard Renzhan was dead, he too posthumously made him Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: When Li Jing heard that Renzhan had died, he too posthumously honored him as Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 壽州故治壽春，世宗以其難克，遂徙城下蔡，而復其軍曰忠正軍，曰：「吾以旌仁贍之節也。」
units.en: Shou Prefecture had once been governed from Shouchun. Shizong, finding the place hard to take, moved the seat to Xiachai and restored the army’s name to the Loyal Upright Army, saying, “I do this to honor Renzhan’s integrity.”
units.literal: Shou Prefecture had formerly been administered from Shouchun. Because Shizong found it hard to capture, he moved the seat to Xiachai and restored the army’s name to the Loyal Upright Army, saying: “I do this to honor Renzhan’s integrity.”

units.en: Discussion
units.literal: 【Discussion】

units.zh: 嗚呼，天下惡梁久矣！
units.en: Alas—the world has hated Liang for ages!
units.literal: Alas, the world has hated Liang for a long time!

units.zh: 然士之不幸而生其時者，不為之臣可也，其食人之祿者，必死人之事，如彥章者，可謂得其死哉！
units.en: Yet for scholars born into that age, refusing office would have been enough; but whoever ate a lord’s salary owed that lord his death. Yanzhang may truly be said to have died as he ought.
units.literal: Yet for gentlemen unlucky enough to be born in that age, not serving as its ministers would have been enough; but those who ate another man’s salary were bound to die for that man’s cause. A man like Yanzhang may truly be said to have died as he ought!

units.zh: 仁贍既殺其子以自明矣，豈有垂死而變節者乎？
units.en: Renzhan had already killed his own son to prove his loyalty—how could he have turned traitor at the point of death?
units.literal: Renzhan had already killed his son to prove his loyalty—how could he have changed his colors on his deathbed?

units.zh: 今《周世宗實錄》載仁贍降書，蓋其副使孫羽等所為也。
units.en: The Veritable Records of Shizong credit Renzhan with a surrender letter—but that was forged by his deputy Sun Yu and the rest.
units.literal: Now the Veritable Records of Emperor Shizong of Zhou record a surrender letter from Renzhan—but that was the work of his deputy Sun Yu and the others.

units.zh: 當世宗時，王環為蜀守秦州，攻之久不下，其力屈而降，世宗頗嗟其忠，然止於為大將軍。
units.en: Under Shizong, Wang Huan held Qin Prefecture for Shu. The siege wore on without result; when his strength gave out he surrendered. Shizong sighed at his loyalty, yet made him only a Grand General.
units.literal: In Shizong’s time Wang Huan held Qin Prefecture for Shu. The siege dragged on without success; when his strength was spent he surrendered. Shizong sighed over his loyalty, yet made him only a Grand General.

units.zh: 視世宗待二人之薄厚而考其制書，乃知仁贍非降者也。
units.en: Weigh how differently Shizong treated the two men and read the edicts he wrote, and you will see Renzhan never surrendered.
units.literal: Compare how thinly or richly Shizong treated the two men and read the edicts he issued, and you will know Renzhan did not surrender.

units.zh: 自古忠臣義士之難得也！
units.en: Since antiquity, loyal ministers and righteous men have been rare indeed!
units.literal: From antiquity, loyal ministers and righteous men have been hard to find!

units.zh: 五代之亂，三人者，或出於軍卒，或出於偽國之臣，可勝嘆哉！
units.en: In the chaos of the Five Dynasties these three—some raised from the ranks, some drawn from the courts of usurper states—how much is there to sigh over!
units.literal: In the chaos of the Five Dynasties these three men—some rising from the ranks of common soldiers, some from the courts of false states—how much is there to sigh over!

units.zh: 可勝嘆哉！
units.en: How much is there to sigh over!
units.literal: How much is there to sigh over!

units.zh: 晉王遣都將李嗣昭、李存審、王建及率師來援同州，戰於城下。
units.en: The Prince of Jin sent Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji to relieve Tongzhou and battle was joined under the walls.
units.literal: The Prince of Jin sent commanders Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji with troops to relieve Tongzhou; they fought below the walls.

units.zh: 夏四月己巳，晉王即唐帝位於魏州，改天祐二十年為同光元年。
units.en: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Prince of Jin took the Tang throne at Weizhou, renaming Tianyou 20 Tongguang 1.
units.literal: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Prince of Jin assumed the Tang throne at Weizhou, changing Tianyou 20 to Tongguang 1.

units.zh: 時晉王方攻鎮州，故思遠乘虛以襲之，陷成安，而思遠遂急攻德勝北城，晉將李存審極力拒守。
units.en: While the Prince of Jin besieged Zhenzhou, Siyuan took Cheng'an and stormed Desheng’s north wall; Li Cunshen held firm.
units.literal: At the time the Prince of Jin was attacking Zhenzhou; hence Siyuan seized the opening to strike, took Cheng'an, and then urgently attacked Desheng’s northern city; Jin commander Li Cunshen resisted with utmost strength.

units.zh: 二月，晉王以兵至，思遠收軍而退，復保楊村。
units.en: In the second month the Prince of Jin came up; Siyuan withdrew to Yang village.
units.literal: In the second month the Prince of Jin arrived with troops; Siyuan gathered the army and withdrew, again holding Yang village.

units.zh: 唐帝棄德勝之北城，並軍保楊劉。
units.en: The Tang emperor abandoned Desheng’s north wall and concentrated at Yangliu.
units.literal: The Tang Emperor abandoned Desheng’s northern city and combined the army to hold Yangliu.

units.zh: 六月乙亥，唐帝引軍援楊劉，潛軍至博州，築壘於河東岸。
units.en: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang emperor relieved Yangliu while secretly fortifying east of Bozhou.
units.literal: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang Emperor led troops to relieve Yangliu, secretly moving the army to Bozhou and building ramparts on the river’s east bank.

units.zh: 秋七月丁未，唐帝引軍沿河而南。
units.en: On dingwei in the seventh month the Tang emperor led his army south along the river.
units.literal: On dingwei in the seventh month of autumn the Tang Emperor led troops south along the river.

units.zh: 庚寅，唐帝軍於胡城，先鋒將康延孝率百騎奔於唐，盡泄其軍機。
units.en: On gengyin at Hucheng vanguard Kang Yanxiao defected with a hundred riders and betrayed Liang dispositions.
units.literal: On gengyin the Tang Emperor’s army was at Hucheng; vanguard commander Kang Yanxiao led a hundred horsemen to defect to Tang and fully revealed our military plans.

units.zh: 甲戌，唐帝引師襲中都，王彥章兵潰，於是彥章與監軍張漢傑及趙廷隱、劉嗣彬、李知節、唐文通、王山興等皆為唐人所獲。
units.en: On jiaxu the Tang emperor stormed Zhongdu; Yanzhang’s army broke; he, Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, and others were taken.
units.literal: On jiaxu the Tang Emperor led troops to strike Zhongdu; Wang Yanzhang’s army collapsed; thereupon Yanzhang, army supervisor Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, Liu Sibin, Li Zhijie, Tang Wentong, Wang Shanxing, and others were all captured by Tang men.

units.zh: 帝置傳國寶於臥內，俄失其所在，已為左右所竊迎唐帝矣。
units.en: He laid the seal in his chamber; it vanished—courtiers had stolen it to greet the Tang emperor.
units.literal: The Emperor placed the dynastic seal in the sleeping chamber; soon it lost its place—it had already been stolen by attendants to welcome the Tang Emperor.

units.zh: 唐帝入宮，妃郭氏號泣迎拜。
units.en: The Tang emperor entered the palace; Consort Guo wept and bowed in welcome.
units.literal: The Tang Emperor entered the palace; consort Guo wailed and came forward to bow.

units.zh: 唐帝初入東京，聞帝殂，憮然歎曰：「敵惠敵怨，不在後嗣。
units.en: Entering the Eastern Capital, the Tang emperor learned of the Last Emperor’s death and sighed: "Grudges need not pass to sons.
units.literal: When the Tang Emperor first entered the Eastern Capital and heard the Emperor had died, he sighed in dejection: "Enemy kindness and enemy hatred do not lie in later generations.

units.zh: 九月庚寅，以供奉官郎公遠充契丹歡好使。
units.en: On gengyin in the ninth month Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was sent as envoy of goodwill to the Khitan.
units.literal: On gengyin in the ninth month, Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was made Khitan Goodwill envoy.

units.zh: 龍德二年春正月，戴思遠率師襲魏州。
units.en: In the first month of Longde 2 Dai Siyuan raided Weizhou.
units.literal: In the first month of spring of Longde 2, Dai Siyuan led troops to raid Weizhou.

units.zh: 尋詔河南尹張全義收葬之，其首藏於太社。
units.en: He ordered Zhang Quanyi to bury the body; the head was kept at the Grand Altar.
units.literal: Soon an edict ordered Henan Intendant Zhang Quanyi to collect and bury him; his head was stored at the Grand Altar.

units.zh: 先是，繼韜父嗣昭為潞州節度使，戰歿於鎮州城下，晉王欲以嗣昭長子繼儔襲父位。
units.en: His father Li Sizhao had held Luzhou and died at Zhenzhou; the Prince of Jin meant to give the post to eldest son Jichou.
units.literal: Earlier, Jiyao’s father Sizhao was Luzhou military commissioner and fell in battle below Zhenzhou city; the Prince of Jin wished to let Sizhao’s eldest son Jichou succeed his father’s post.

units.zh: 朕與梁主十年對壘，恨不生見其面。」
units.en: We fought ten years; I regret never meeting him alive."
units.literal: I and the Liang ruler faced each other in battle ten years, regretting I did not see his face in life."

units.zh: 以天雄軍節度使石敬瑭為御營使。
units.en: Shi Jingtang of Tianxiong became imperial camp commissioner.
units.literal: Tianxiong army military commissioner Shi Jingtang was made imperial camp commissioner.

units.zh: 乙酉，前蔡州刺史董璋權知宣義軍軍州事。
units.en: On yiyou, Dong Zhang, former prefect of Cai, was given acting charge of Xuanyi Army affairs.
units.literal: On yiyou, former Cai prefect Dong Zhang was made acting Xuanyi Army military and prefectural commissioner.

units.zh: 二月甲申，晉王攻我黎陽，劉鄩拒之而退。
units.en: On jiashen in the second month, the Prince of Jin attacked Liyang; Liu Xun held him off and forced a withdrawal.
units.literal: On jiashen in the second month, the Prince of Jin attacked our Liyang; Liu Xun resisted him and drove him back.

units.zh: 貞明三年春正月戊午，以前淄州刺史高允奇為右羽林統軍。
units.en: On wuwu in the first month of Zhenming 3, Gao Yunqi, former Inspector of Zi Prefecture, was appointed commander of the Right Feathered Forest.
units.literal: On wuwu, in the first month of spring of Zhenming 3, former Zi Prefecture Inspector Gao Yunqi was made commander of the Right Feathered Forest.

units.zh: 復領兵萬餘人渡淮討楊行密，至濠州，聞龐師古清口之敗，遽班師。
units.en: Crossing the Huai against Yang Xingmi he withdrew on news of Qingkou.
units.literal: Again he led more than ten thousand troops across the Huai to attack Yang Xingmi; reaching Haozhou he heard of Pang Shigu's defeat at Qingkou and hastily withdrew the army.

units.zh: 仁贍輕財重士，法令嚴肅，重圍之中，其子崇諫犯軍禁，即令斬之，故能以一城之眾，連年拒守。
units.en: Renshan was light with wealth and heavy toward scholars; his laws were stern; in the tight siege his son Chongjian violated military law and he at once had him beheaded—therefore with one city's troops he could hold out for years.
units.literal: Renshan was light with wealth and heavy toward scholars; his laws were stern; in the tight siege his son Chongjian violated military prohibition and he at once ordered him beheaded—therefore with the troops of one city he could hold out for years.

units.zh: 初，樞自歙州罷郡歸朝，路經大梁，時硃全忠兵威已振，樞以兄事之，全忠由是重之。
units.en: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.
units.literal: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.

units.zh: 制出，硃全忠保薦之，言樞有經世才，不可棄之嶺表，尋復拜門下侍郎，監修國史，累兼吏部尚書，判度支。
units.en: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed vice minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as minister of personnel, administering the treasury.
units.literal: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as Minister of Personnel, administering the treasury.

units.zh: 及樞傳詔，全忠皆稟朝旨，獻奉相繼，昭宗甚悅，遷兵部侍郎。
units.en: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to vice minister of war.
units.literal: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 時崔胤專政，亦倚全忠，二人因是相結，改樞吏部侍郎。
units.en: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to vice minister of personnel.
units.literal: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 崔胤誅，以全忠素厚，相位如故。
units.en: After Cui Yin's execution, Shu's ties to Quanzhong kept him in the chancellorship unchanged.
units.literal: When Cui Yin was executed, because of his longstanding closeness to Quanzhong Shu's chancellorship remained unchanged.

units.zh: 先是，李景遣其弟偽齊王達率全軍來援壽州，達留駐濠州，遣其將許文縝、邊鎬、朱元領兵數萬，溯淮而上，至紫金山，設十餘寨，與城內烽火相應。
units.en: Earlier Li Jing had sent his brother, the puppet Prince of Qi Da, at the head of the full Southern Tang army to relieve Shouzhou. Da stayed at Haozhou and dispatched Xu Wenzhen, Bian Hao, and Zhu Yuan with tens of thousands of men up the Huai to Purple Gold Mountain, where they pitched more than ten camps linked by beacon fire to the besieged city.
units.literal: Earlier, Li Jing had sent his younger brother, the unrecognized Prince of Qi, Da, leading the full army to relieve Shouzhou; Da remained at Haozhou and sent his generals Xu Wenzhen, Bian Hao, and Zhu Yuan with tens of thousands of troops up the Huai to Purple Gold Mountain, establishing more than ten camps in beacon contact with the city.

units.zh: 次均王友貞，為東都馬步都指揮使。
units.en: Next was Prince of Jun Youzhen, commander of horse and foot at the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: Next was Prince of Jun Youzhen, Eastern Capital Horse and Foot Commander.

units.zh: 遣供奉官丁昭溥馳詣東都，命均王友貞殺友文。
units.en: He sent palace attendant Ding Zhaopu in haste to the Eastern Capital to order Prince of Jun Youzhen to kill Youwen.
units.literal: He dispatched Palace Attendant Ding Zhaopu posthaste to the Eastern Capital ordering Prince of Jun Youzhen to kill Youwen.

units.zh: 梁祖在位止及六年，均帝朝詔史臣修梁祖實錄，岐下系鞋之事，恥而不書。
units.en: Taizu reigned only six years; under Emperor Jun historians were ordered to compile his veritable record—yet the shoe-tying at Qi was too shameful to write.
units.literal: Liang Taizu reigned only six years; in Emperor Jun’s reign an edict ordered historians to compile Taizu’s veritable record—the affair of tying shoes below Qi was shameful and not written.

units.zh: 辛巳，丁昭溥還，聞友文已死，乃發喪，宣遺制，友珪即皇帝位。
units.en: On xinsi Ding Zhaopu returned; learning Youwen was dead, they announced mourning, proclaimed the testament, and Yougui seized the throne.
units.literal: On xinsi Ding Zhaopu returned; hearing Youwen was already dead, they then announced the mourning, proclaimed the testamentary order, and Yougui at once took the throne.

units.zh: 丙戌，以宣徽北院使兼樞密副使鄭仁誨為澶州節度使，以殿前都指揮使李重進領泗州防禦使，以客省使向訓為內客省使。
units.en: On bingxu Zheng Renhui (Northern Palace Secretariat and vice military affairs commissioner) took Chanzhou; Palace Front commander Li Chongjin took Sizhou; and reception commissioner Xiang Xun became inner reception commissioner.
units.literal: On bingxu, Zheng Renhui, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made military governor of Chanzhou; Li Chongjin, commander-in-chief of the Palace Front Division, was given charge of Sizhou as defense commissioner; and Xiang Xun, commissioner of the Reception Bureau, was made commissioner of the Inner Reception Bureau.

units.zh: 丁酉，以滑州節度使兼殿前都點檢、駙馬都尉張永德為澶州節度使，加檢校太尉；
units.en: On dingyou, Zhang Yongde, Huazhou commissioner, Director of the Palace Front, and imperial son-in-law, was made Chanzhou commissioner and acting Grand Marshal;
units.literal: On the day dingyou, Zhang Yongde, military commissioner of Huazhou, concurrent Director of the Palace Front, and Commander of the Imperial Sons-in-law, was made military commissioner of Chanzhou and advanced to acting Grand Marshal;

units.zh: 龍德三年春三月，晉潞州節度留後李繼韜遣使以城歸順。
units.en: In the third month of Longde 3 Li Jiyao of Luzhou offered the city to Liang.
units.literal: In the third month of spring of Longde 3, Jin Luzhou military retention commissioner Li Jiyao sent envoys offering the city in submission.

units.zh: 繼韜在潞州，即執繼儔囚之，遣使來送款，仍以二幼子為質。
units.en: Jiyao imprisoned Jichou, submitted to Liang, and sent two sons as hostages.
units.literal: Jiyao was at Luzhou; he thereupon seized Jichou and imprisoned him, sent envoys to offer allegiance, and also sent two young sons as hostages.

units.zh: 澤州刺史裴約不從繼韜之謀，帝命董璋為澤州刺史，令將兵攻之。
units.en: Ze prefect Pei Yue refused the plot; Dong Zhang was sent to take Ze by force.
units.literal: Ze prefect Pei Yue did not follow Jiyao’s plot; the Emperor ordered Dong Zhang made Ze prefect and commanded him to lead troops to attack.

units.zh: 是月，周主威殂，養子晉王柴榮嗣立。
units.en: That month Zhou's ruler Guo Wei died, and his adopted son, Prince of Jin Chai Rong, succeeded him.
units.literal: That month Zhou ruler Wei died; his adopted son, Prince of Jin Chai Rong, succeeded to the throne.

units.zh: 是月，周主榮殂，子宗訓立。
units.en: That month Zhou's ruler Rong died and his son Zongxun succeeded to the throne.
units.literal: That month, Zhou's ruler Rong died and his son Zongxun succeeded to the throne.

units.zh: 時租庸使趙岩勸帝郊天，且言：「帝王受命，須行此禮，願陛下力行之。」
units.en: Rent and Corvée commissioner Zhao Yan urged Heaven-sacrifice, saying: "Emperors who receive the Mandate must perform this rite—Your Majesty should see it through."
units.literal: At the time Rent and Corvée commissioner Zhao Yan urged the Emperor to sacrifice to Heaven, saying: "When emperors receive the Mandate they must perform this rite; Your Majesty should exert yourself to carry it out."

units.zh: 十二月，晉王自太原復至魏州。
units.en: In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin returned from Taiyuan to Weizhou.
units.literal: In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin came again from Taiyuan to Weizhou.

units.zh: 己巳，帝幸洛陽，為來年有事於南郊也。
units.en: On jisi the Emperor went to Luoyang to prepare for a Southern Suburban rite the following year.
units.literal: On jisi the Emperor visited Luoyang, because next year there would be affairs at the Southern Suburban Altar.

units.zh: 乙巳，杀李景之臣孙晟。
units.en: On yisi Sun Sheng, a Southern Tang minister of Li Jing, was put to death.
units.literal: On yisi Sun Sheng, a minister of Li Jing, was executed.

units.zh: 時李嗣源總帳下親軍攻東北隅；
units.en: Li Siyuan led the household guard against the northeast corner;
units.literal: Li Siyuan commanded the personal troops below the tent attacking the northeast corner;

units.zh: 李嗣源壞夾城東北隅，率先掩擊，梁軍大恐，南向而奔，投戈委甲，噎塞行路，斬萬餘級，獲其將副招討使符道昭洎大將三百人，芻粟百萬。
units.en: Li Siyuan breached Jiacity's northeast and charged in; Liang panicked and fled south, shedding arms until the road jammed; over ten thousand were killed; Fu Daozhao and three hundred officers were taken, with a million bundles of fodder.
units.literal: Li Siyuan broke the northeast corner of Jiacity and led the assault; the Liang army was greatly terrified and fled south, casting weapons and armor; the road was choked; more than ten thousand were beheaded; deputy pacification commissioner Fu Daozhao and three hundred great generals were captured, and a million measures of fodder.

units.zh: 五月辛未朔，晨霧晦暝，帝率親軍伏三垂崗下。
units.en: At the xinwei new moon in the fifth month, thick morning fog hid Cunxu's personal troops below Sanchui Ridge.
units.literal: On the first day xinwei of the fifth month, morning fog dark and dim, the Emperor led his personal army in ambush below Sanchui Ridge.

units.zh: 六月，遣兗州節度使劉鄩、華州節度使尹皓、崇州節度使溫昭圖、莊宅使段凝領軍攻同州。
units.en: In the sixth month Liu Yan of Yan, Yin Hao of Hua, Wen Zhaotu of Chong, and Duan Ning of the Manor Estates marched on Tongzhou.
units.literal: In the sixth month, Yanzhou military commissioner Liu Yan, Huazhou military commissioner Yin Hao, Chongzhou military commissioner Wen Zhaotu, and Manor Estates commissioner Duan Ning led armies to attack Tongzhou.

units.zh: 八月，段凝、張朗攻衛州，下之，獲刺史李存儒以獻。
units.en: In the eighth month Duan Ning and Zhang Lang took Weizhou and sent captive commissioner Li Cunru to court.
units.literal: In the eighth month Duan Ning and Zhang Lang attacked Weizhou and took it, capturing military commissioner Li Cunru and presenting him.

units.zh: 己巳，王彥章、段凝圍楊劉城。
units.en: On jisi Wang Yanzhang and Duan Ning besieged Yangliu.
units.literal: On jisi, Wang Yanzhang and Duan Ning besieged Yangliu city.

units.zh: 八月，以段凝代王彥章為北面行營招討使。
units.en: In the eighth month Duan Ning replaced Wang Yanzhang as northern commander.
units.literal: In the eighth month Duan Ning replaced Wang Yanzhang as Northern Campaign Pacification commissioner.

units.zh: 戊子，段凝營於王村，引軍自高陵渡河，復臨河而還。
units.en: On wuzi Duan Ning camped at Wang village, crossed at Gaoling, and maneuvered along the river.
units.literal: On wuzi, Duan Ning encamped at Wang village, led troops from Gaoling to cross the river, and again faced the river returning.

units.zh: 帝聞中都之敗，唐軍長驅將至，遣張漢倫馳驛召段凝於河上；
units.en: Hearing of Zhongdu’s fall and Tang’s advance, the Emperor dispatched Zhang Hanlun to recall Duan Ning from the river;
units.literal: The Emperor heard of Zhongdu’s defeat and that Tang troops were coming at speed; he sent Zhang Hanlun by post relay to summon Duan Ning on the river;

units.zh: 時禁軍尚有四千人，朱圭請以拒唐軍，帝不從，登建國門召開封尹王瓚，謂之曰：「段凝未至，社稷係卿方略。」
units.en: Four thousand guards remained; Zhu Gui begged to fight; the Emperor refused, climbed the Founding Gate, called Wang Zan, and said: "Until Duan Ning comes the realm rests on you."
units.literal: At the time the Imperial Guard still had four thousand men; Zhu Gui asked to use them to resist Tang troops; the Emperor did not follow, ascended the Founding Gate, summoned Kaifeng Intendant Wang Zan, and said to him: "Duan Ning has not arrived—the altars depend on your strategy."

units.zh: 戊子，以前右龍武軍都虞候、守左龍武大將軍李紹奇為鄭州防禦使，以楚州防禦使張繼孫為汝州防禦使。
units.en: On wuzi Li Shaoqi became Zheng defender and Zhang Jisun Ruzhou defender.
units.literal: On wuzi former Right Dragon Martial chief of staff and acting Left Dragon Martial general Li Shaoqi was made Zhengzhou defender; Chuzhou defender Zhang Jisun was made Ruzhou defender.

units.zh: 丙午，壽州劉仁贍上表乞降，帝遣閣門使張保績入城慰撫。
units.en: On bingwu, Liu Renzan of Shouzhou petitioned to surrender; the Emperor sent Zhang Baoji of the Gate Department into the city to reassure him.
units.literal: On the day bingwu, Liu Renzan of Shouzhou submitted a memorial begging to surrender; the Emperor sent Zhang Baoji of the Gate Department into the city to comfort and reassure him.

units.zh: 翌日，仁贍復令子崇讓上表請罪。
units.en: The next day Renzan had his son Chongrang submit a further memorial asking to be punished.
units.literal: The next day Renzan again had his son Chongrang submit a memorial requesting punishment.

units.zh: 辛亥，以偽命清淮軍節度使、檢校太尉、兼侍中劉仁贍為特進、檢校太尉、兼中書令、鄆州節度使，以右羽林統軍楊信為壽州節度使。
units.en: On xinhai, Liu Renzan, the Southern Tang-appointed Qinghuai commissioner, was named Special Advancement, acting Grand Marshal, Director of the Secretariat, and Yunzhou commissioner; Yang Xin of the Right Imperial Guard was made Shouzhou commissioner.
units.literal: On the day xinhai, Liu Renzan, military commissioner of Qinghuai Army by usurper appointment, acting Grand Marshal and concurrent Palace Attendant, was made Special Advancement, acting Grand Marshal, concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and military commissioner of Yunzhou; Yang Xin, commander of the Right Imperial Guard, was made military commissioner of Shouzhou.

units.zh: 戊申，幸壽州城北，劉仁贍與將佐已下及兵士萬餘人出降，帝慰勞久之，恩賜有差。
units.en: On wushen, the Emperor went to the north side of Shouzhou, where Liu Renzan, his staff, and more than ten thousand troops came out to surrender. The Emperor received them with lengthy words of comfort and granted rewards according to rank.
units.literal: On the day wushen, he visited the north of Shouzhou city; Liu Renzan with his officers and more than ten thousand soldiers came out to surrender; the Emperor comforted them at length and bestowed favors in graded amounts.

units.zh: 是日，劉仁贍卒。
units.en: That same day Liu Renzan died.
units.literal: That same day Liu Renzan died.

units.zh: 甲戌，賜左監門上將軍許文縝、右千牛上將軍邊鎬、右衛大將軍王環、衛尉卿周延構、太府卿馮延魯、太僕卿鄭牧、鴻臚卿孫羽、衛尉少卿鐘謨、工部郎中何幼沖各冬服絹二百匹、綿五百兩。
units.en: On jiaxu, Xu Wenzhen, Bian Hao, Wang Huan, Zhou Yanguo, Feng Yanlu, Zheng Mu, Sun Yu, Zhong Mo, and He Youchong of the Ministry of Works each received two hundred bolts of winter silk and five hundred liang of cotton.
units.literal: On the day jiaxu, Xu Wenzhen, senior general of the Left Gate Guards; Bian Hao, senior general of the Right Imperial Stud; Wang Huan, grand general of the Right Guard; Zhou Yangou, Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud; Feng Yanlu, Minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury; Zheng Mu, Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; Sun Yu, Minister of the Court for Diplomatic Reception; Zhong Mo, Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud; and He Youchong, director in the Ministry of Works — each was granted two hundred bolts of winter silk and five hundred liang of cotton.

units.zh: 文縝已下，皆吳、蜀之士也。
units.en: Wenzhen and the others were all former subjects of Wu and Shu.
units.literal: From Wenzhen downward, all were men of Wu and Shu.

units.zh: 因召吳珙、李存璋、李存敬、朱守殷諭其謀，眾鹹憤怒。
units.en: He called Wu Gong, Li Cunzhang, Li Cunjing, and Zhu Shouyin; all raged.
units.literal: He then summoned Wu Gong, Li Cunzhang, Li Cunjing, and Zhu Shouyin to explain the plot; all were furious.

units.zh: 二月壬戌，命存璋伏甲以誅克寧，遂靖其難。
units.en: On renxu in the second month Cunzhang ambushed and killed Kening, ending the crisis.
units.literal: On renxu in the second month he ordered Cunzhang with hidden armor to execute Kening and thus settled the trouble.

units.zh: 故昭義節度使李嗣昭、故幽州節度使周德威、故汴州節度使符存審，並配饗莊宗廟廷。
units.en: Li Sizhao, Zhou Dewei, and Fu Cunshen were given collateral offerings in Zhuangzong's temple.
units.literal: The late Zhaoyi military commissioner Li Sizhao, late Youzhou military commissioner Zhou Dewei, late Bianzhou military commissioner Fu Cunshen—all were collaterally offered in Zhuangzong's temple hall.

units.zh: 乙太府卿敬翔知崇政院，翔與帷幄之謀，故首擢焉。
units.en: Grand Master of Splendid Affairs Jing Xiang was put in charge of the Chongzhengyuan—first among promotions because he had shared the Emperor's counsels in the field.
units.literal: Appointing Grand Master of Splendid Affairs Jing Xiang to oversee the Chongzhengyuan; Xiang had shared in secret planning within the tent, hence he was first promoted.

units.zh: 可改唐天祐四年為開平元年，國號大樑。
units.en: Let Tang's Tianyou year 4 become Kaiping year 1; the realm shall be called Great Liang.
units.literal: Let the fourth year of Tang's Tianyou be changed to the first year of Kaiping; the state name is Great Liang.

units.zh: 壬子，中書門下奏：「詳覆到禮部院今年及第進士李飛、樊吉、夏侯珙、吳沺、王德柔、李穀等六人，望放及第。
units.en: On renzi the Secretariat said: "After review, this year's six passed candidates Li Fei, Fan Ji, Xiahou Gong, Wu Dian, Wang Derou, and Li Gu should be graduated.
units.literal: On renzi the Secretariat memorialized: "Upon review at the Ministry of Rites this year's passed jinshi Li Fei, Fan Ji, Xiahou Gong, Wu Dian, Wang Derou, and Li Gu—six men—are wished to be released as passed.

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: Approved.
units.literal: It was approved.

units.zh: 丙寅，以西面行營馬軍都指揮使、檢校太保、鄭州刺史、充本州防禦使王彥章為檢校太傅。
units.en: On bingyin, Wang Yanzhang, Western Line horse commander, honorary Grand Guardian, and Zheng prefect and defense commissioner, was promoted to honorary Grand Mentor.
units.literal: On bingyin, Western Line camp horse commander, honorary Grand Guardian, Zheng prefect, and Zheng defense commissioner Wang Yanzhang was made honorary Grand Mentor.

units.zh: 友能走保陳州，詔張漢傑率兵進討。
units.en: You Neng shut himself in Chenzhou; Zhang Hanjie was ordered to besiege him.
units.literal: You Neng fled to hold Chenzhou; an edict ordered Zhang Hanjie to lead troops forward to attack.

units.zh: 其行營將士賞賚已給付本家，宜令招討使霍彥威、副招討使王彥章、陳州行營都指揮使張漢傑曉示諸軍知委。」
units.en: Campaign bonuses sent to soldiers’ families should be announced by Huo Yanwei, Wang Yanzhang, and Zhang Hanjie."
units.literal: Campaign soldiers’ rewards already paid to their families—the Pacification commissioner Huo Yanwei, deputy Pacification commissioner Wang Yanzhang, and Chenzhou campaign commander-in-chief Zhang Hanjie should announce to all armies for their knowledge."

units.zh: 董璋攻澤州，下之。
units.en: Dong Zhang took Ze prefecture.
units.literal: Dong Zhang attacked Ze prefecture and took it.

units.zh: 後以其子崇讃為懷州刺史。
units.en: Later his son Chongzan was made prefect of Huai.
units.literal: Later his son Chongzan was made prefect of Huai.

units.zh: 崇贊仕周，累為郡守。
units.en: Chongzan served Zhou and successively governed prefectures.
units.literal: Chongzan served Zhou and successively held prefectures.

units.zh: 幼子崇諒，後自江南歸於本朝，亦位至省郎。
units.en: His youngest son Chongliang later returned from Jiangnan to the court and also rose to a secretariat post.
units.literal: His youngest son Chongliang later returned from Jiangnan to the court and also rose to a post in the secretariat.

units.zh: 十二月乙卯，泗州守将范再遇叛 于唐，以其州来降。
units.en: On yimao in the twelfth month Si Prefecture commander Fan Zaiyu turned on Southern Tang and surrendered his prefecture.
units.literal: On yimao in the twelfth month Fan Zaiyu, garrison commander of Si Prefecture, rebelled against Tang and surrendered the prefecture.

units.zh: 身居其地而来降者书「附」，再遇、廷谓虽以地降，既降而不居其地，故不书「附」而书「降」。廷谓不书「叛」，事见南唐世家。
units.en: Defectors who still held their posts are recorded as “attached.” Zaiyu and Tingwei surrendered territory but did not stay to hold it, so the text says “surrendered” rather than “attached.” Tingwei is not called a “rebel”; see the Southern Tang house chronicle.
units.literal: Those who lived in the territory and came to submit are recorded with “attached.” Although Zaiyu and Tingwei surrendered their prefectures, once they surrendered they did not remain in their territory, and so the text does not say “attached” but says “surrendered.” Tingwei is not recorded as “rebelled”; the matter is treated in the Southern Tang house chronicle.
